page: Microsoft Azure D8alds_v6 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Daldv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The memory configuration is constrained to 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth is highly asymmetric; while cached small-block read-only bandwidth is average at 608.08 GB/sec, uncached large-block read-only bandwidth is weak, scoring in the bottom 25% at 39.09 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth remains average at 27.76 GB/sec.

This instance is suited for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints, such as text processing, static web serving, and lightweight database operations. The presence of a 472 GB local NVMe SSD supports workloads requiring fast local scratch space. However, the low memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core and weak uncached memory read bandwidth present clear tradeoffs, making it less suitable for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM inference, as evidenced by weak prompt processing speeds on 7B parameter models.
description: Microsoft Azure D8alds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a 472 GB local NVMe SSD. With a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this instance is tailored for compute-focused workloads rather than memory-heavy tasks. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, placing in the top 25%, while multi-core metrics and database operations fall in the average range. However, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is weak, representing a key hardware tradeoff. The bundled NVMe storage and dedicated CPU allocation make it suitable for static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations that benefit from fast local disk access but do not require extensive memory capacity.
